label: pp-sentry-agent-platform
topic: Sentry as a platform for agents to communicate
summary: I could not identify an agent-to-agent communication platform called Sentry. The well-known Sentry (sentry.io) is error monitoring. It offers a hosted MCP server (https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp, OAuth login) that lets an AI assistant query a Sentry account, and agent observability features (agent tracing, Conversations beta), but I found no feature that routes messages between agents. Separate, unaffiliated products do agent-to-agent messaging: AgentDM (MCP-based, CLI creates an agent and API key) and MCP Agent Mail (open-source, per-agent inboxes). Repo search of delphisci found only ISSUES.md line 164 (an open "identify Sentry" issue, blocked) and a helper script mention; replies.md has no mention. Nothing was logged into or created. Note: the minimal JSON written to the output path is a stub; this structured return is the full result.
lay_summary: You said Sentry is a place where agents talk to each other. I could not find that. The famous Sentry is a tool that records software crashes, a bit like a flight recorder for programs. It can be plugged into an AI assistant so the assistant can read those crash reports, but that is the assistant looking things up, not agents chatting. Other products really are like a mailbox for AI agents, and one of them may be what you remember. I did not sign up or log in to anything. One question from you will settle which it is.

Which Sentry the user meant: needs user answer. Three likely candidates: (1) sentry.io plus its MCP server, used earlier to read errors; (2) AgentDM or MCP Agent Mail, an actual agent-messaging product misnamed; (3) a private or lab-internal tool nicknamed Sentry (e.g. a collaborator's swarm). Distinguishing question: what did you do with it before, and where did you log in or what URL, command or config did you use?
Connection info needed: base URL, auth type (OAuth/API key/webhook), account or org owner, names or aliases of the other agents
recommendations: Ask Amit the one distinguishing question: what URL or command did he use last time, and did it involve crash reports (candidate 1), agent aliases/inboxes (candidate 2) or a collaborator's private setup (candidate 3)?
